sources.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08
sources.locator: Ch. 2 Example 2.39 p.39; Ch. 4 pp.68–82; Ch. 8 Theorem 8.43 pp.151–152
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted the complete 166-page PDF. Inspected the full relevant Ch. 4 lattice, volume, ideal-norm, class-bound, application and example arguments on printed pp.68–82; Ch. 2 Example 2.39; and the complete Hermite proof on printed pp.151–152. The PDF uses unscaled real/imaginary coordinates. The totally complex Hermite window restricts the first real coordinate and enlarges its imaginary coordinate.

contents.name: Proposition 4.1: relative ideal norm and principal ideals
contents.reason: The relative ideal-norm construction for arbitrary extensions is beyond this page; NT-22 uses the already published absolute number-field norm interface.

contents.name: Proposition 4.2(a): absolute ideal norm multiplicativity
contents.support: Numerical ideal norm and product formula are already published and examined before the class-bound proof.
contents.reason: Already published as thm-ideal-norm-is-multiplicative and used only as an examined prerequisite; this batch does not reprove it.

contents.name: Theorem 4.3: integral representative in every ideal class
contents.support: The proof applies small-element to an inverse ideal and checks the resulting class direction.

contents.name: Examples 4.5 and 4.6: Gaussian and Q(√−5) class groups
contents.support: Example 4.5 also supports the separate Gaussian B item; Example 4.6 gives the norm-two generator and nonprincipality.

contents.name: Example 4.7: small-discriminant cubic fields
contents.reason: This extra cubic sample duplicates the higher-degree worked enumeration; the selected B example uses the quintic where norms two and three are explicitly excluded.

contents.name: Example 4.8: quintic X^5−X+1 class-number computation
contents.support: The sign-changed polynomial X^5−X−1 defines the same field and has the same squarefree discriminant; both F2 and F3 norm exclusions are proved in the B strategy.

contents.name: Theorem 4.9: no nontrivial unramified extension of Q
Corollary 4.10: no monic irreducible degree>1 with discriminant ±1
contents.reason: This polynomial-order reformulation is a direct application of the field discriminant bound; the A page retains the number-field claim and the B page illustrates it.

contents.name: Remarks 4.11–4.12: Hilbert class fields and class towers
contents.reason: Existence and Galois description of Hilbert class fields need class field theory, which is outside NT-22 and not a premise of its finiteness proof.

contents.name: Lemma 4.14 and Proposition 4.15: lattice discreteness
contents.support: The scaffold proves the needed bounded-point direction by integer basis coordinates; no converse classification is claimed.

contents.name: Remark 4.18 and Theorem 4.19: Minkowski strict and equality forms
contents.support: The equality limit is separated into its own corollary.

contents.name: Theorem 4.19 equality limit for compact bodies
Remark 4.20: four-square application
contents.reason: The four-square theorem is an additive arithmetic application of Minkowski, already outside the assigned lattice and number-field class-group inventory.

contents.name: Lemma 4.25: finite AM–GM
contents.support: The published nonnegative finite AM–GM inequality is used with two copies of each complex modulus.
contents.reason: Already published as thm-am-gm and used only as an examined prerequisite; this batch does not reprove it.

contents.name: Proposition 4.26: ideal embedding and covolume
contents.support: Its full-rank part also supports the earlier ideal-lattice theorem.

contents.name: Proposition 4.26: full lattice of a number-field ideal
Example 2.39: squarefree-discriminant quintic
contents.support: Irreducibility modulo three and squarefree discriminant establish the maximal order used by the B example.

contents.name: Theorem 8.42: extensions unramified outside finite S
contents.reason: Its relative-field ramification and local extension classification exceed the fixed-degree absolute Hermite theorem assigned to this A page.

contents.name: Theorem 8.43: Hermite finiteness and asymmetric windows
contents.support: The two window volumes and unique exceptional embedding supply a bounded primitive generator.

sources.title: William A. Stein, Algebraic Number Theory: A Computational Approach
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted the complete 215-page book. Inspected the complete §6.3 norm and bounded-ideal arguments, the complete §7.1 Minkowski/class-bound proof including its stated unproved calculus optimization, and §7.3 small-prime examples on printed pp.84–85. Stein’s fractional-ideal index wording is not used as a literal finite group index.

contents.name: Definition 6.3.2 and Lemma 6.3.3: fractional ideal norm and scaling
contents.support: The scaffold applies multiplicativity only to the integral ideals a,b and the principal ideal (β), avoiding fractional finite-index notation.

contents.name: Proposition 6.3.4: norm multiplicativity
contents.reason: Already published as thm-ideal-norm-is-multiplicative and used only as an examined prerequisite; this batch does not reprove it.

contents.name: Proposition 6.3.6: finite ideals of bounded norm
Definition 7.1.1: class group
contents.reason: Already published as def-ideal-class-group-of-a-domain and used only as an examined prerequisite; this batch does not reprove it.

contents.name: Theorem 7.1.2: class bound and finiteness
contents.support: The proof obtains the inverse-class multiplier and a general convex body constant; the explicit optimum is left to calculus, supplied by Milne and Conrad.

contents.name: Examples 7.1.3–7.1.4: Gaussian and Q(√10)
contents.support: The Q(√10) relation and norm-equation obstruction are fully worked; Gaussian has a separate B row.

contents.name: Lemma 7.1.6: lattice index and covolume
contents.support: Used only for an actual integral inclusion of full lattices, where index is defined as a finite quotient.

contents.name: Lemma 7.3.1: generation by small prime ideals
Examples 7.3.2–7.3.4: Gaussian, Q(√5), Q(√−6)
contents.reason: The additional Q(√5) and Q(√−6) computations are sound worked examples but the assigned B inventory already fixes Gaussian, Q(√−5), Q(√10) and one quintic.

sources.title: Brian Conrad and Aaron Landesman, Math 154 Algebraic Number Theory
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted the complete 153-page lecture-note set. Inspected the §25 class-group computations, §26 inverse-ideal relation and embedding, §27 determinant/volume and product-region calculations, and §28 complete Blichfeldt/Minkowski argument through printed p.147. §28 states Hermite and refers its proof elsewhere; Milne supplies that proof.

contents.name: Definition 25.1 and Theorem 25.2: Minkowski constant and class representatives
Examples 25.4–25.8: quadratic class group calculations
contents.reason: These additional quadratic fields illustrate relation finding but are not in the assigned seven-example B inventory; the source method informs its Q(√10) calculation.

contents.name: Example 26.1: real quadratic Q(√82) class group
contents.reason: The Q(√82) computation requires a separate unit-group argument and a homework norm obstruction; NT-22 instead assigns Q(√10) with a short congruence proof.

contents.name: Theorem 26.2: small element and inverse-class deduction
contents.support: The displayed inverse-class argument also supports the exact direction in the class bound.

contents.name: Lemma 27.2: determinant covolume and unimodular invariance
Theorem 28.4: Hermite finiteness
contents.support: The notes state Hermite and refer Samuel for proof; Milne’s complete asymmetric-window argument supports the actual local proof.

contents.name: Theorem 28.5: bounded ramification extensions over a fixed base
contents.reason: The relative-field finite-ramification theorem requires local ramification theory and is stronger in a different direction than assigned Hermite finiteness.

sources.title: Ben Green, Additive Combinatorics, Lecture 3 §3.7
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted the complete 13-page lecture chapter. Inspected the full §3.7 Blichfeldt proof, successive-minima setup and centroid-triangular proof of the upper bound on printed pp.26–28, plus its Bohr-set application on pp.28–29. The proof uses Blichfeldt directly on the transformed image; it does not establish that image is convex.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3: centroid slices and triangular Jacobian
contents.support: The scaffold spells out Borel fibre measurability, triangular volume scaling and absence of 2Λ-collisions.

contents.name: Corollary 3.2: Bohr sets contain proper progressions
contents.reason: This is a combinatorial application reserved by the combinatorics track for a future sumset/Freiman page; NT-22 supplies only its exact Minkowski-second-theorem input.

sources.title: Martin Henk, Successive Minima and Lattice Points
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted the complete seven-page author paper. Inspected the successive-minima definitions and first/second theorem statements, the lattice-point enumerator section, and the full independent slicing/volume proof of the second-theorem upper bound on pp.5–7. The paper does not give the cross-polytope lower bound, which is proved locally.

contents.name: Theorem 1.2: Minkowski first theorem on minima
contents.support: The first-minimum consequence is absorbed by the local convex-body theorem and minima definition.

contents.name: Theorem 1.3 and §3 proof: second-theorem upper bound
contents.support: This is an independent full upper-bound proof using disjoint translates and section volume inequalities.

contents.name: Conjecture 1.4: lattice-point enumerator product bound
contents.reason: The conjectural discrete lattice-point bound is not established by this source and is not promised by NT-22; no theorem is scaffolded from it.

contents.name: Theorem 1.5 and Lemma 2.1: lattice-point enumerator estimate
contents.reason: This stronger count of lattice points is not required for the class group or the planned combinatorics seam; the page keeps the continuous second-theorem bounds.

canonical.name: Unscaled Minkowski embedding convention
canonical.support: The unscaled convention assigns equal weight to real and imaginary coordinates, so a complex block has norm sqrt(sum_j |tau_j(x)|^2). The all-embedding determinant theorem and the modulus-2 row transition for each complex pair give the realified determinant factor 2^{-r2}.

canonical.name: Triangular Borel shears preserve fibre volume
canonical.support: The standard Tonelli and one-dimensional translation argument is isolated before the nonlinear deformation.

canonical.name: Full two-sided successive-minima inequality
canonical.support: Green and Henk supply the upper bound; the cross-polytope lower bound is proved explicitly.

canonical.name: Finite bounded-conjugate polynomial box
canonical.support: The Vieta coefficient bound is extracted from Milne’s Hermite proof.

canonical.name: Class group finite by bounded representatives
canonical.support: The finite representative map is the immediate consequence of the class bound and bounded-ideal lemma.

canonical.name: Q(√10) class group by norm 2 and 3 ideals
canonical.support: Stein gives the complete real quadratic computation; the scaffold uses the shorter norm-six relation.

canonical.name: Discriminant signature estimate example
canonical.support: The B calculation spells out the n=2 constants and the general signature inequality.

canonical.name: Unramified-over-Q example
canonical.support: The B example restates the finite-prime consequence with its discriminant route.

canonical.name: Scaled-convention counterexample
canonical.support: The disk in √2Z² explicitly falsifies a mixed-covolume threshold, without questioning Minkowski’s true theorem.
